summary: Searches the null-terminated haystack string a1 for the two-byte pattern stored at a2 (bytes a2[0] and a2[1], i.e. fields this+0 and this+1). Returns a pointer to the match start, returns a1 unchanged when the pattern's first byte is empty, and returns 0 when the haystack is exhausted without a match. A single-byte pattern falls through to a tail-jump continuation at 0x589DB6.

local_names.v3: current match-candidate start in the haystack

operations.description: Load the first pattern byte v2 = a2[0] (field this+0).
If the pattern is empty (a2[0] == 0), return a1 unchanged.
Load the second pattern byte v4 = a2[1] (field this+1).
If the pattern has only one byte (v4 == 0), tail-jump to the continuation block at 0x589DB6 for the single-byte search path.
Scan the haystack for the first pattern byte v2, advancing v6 one byte at a time.
When a candidate byte equals v2, check the following haystack byte against v4; on failure restart the outer scan.
Verify the remaining pattern byte pairs (v5[2]/v5[3], then two bytes further each iteration) against the haystack, stepping two bytes at a time; a mismatching pair restarts the outer scan (LABEL_3).
Return the match start pointer (v3 - 1) on full pattern match, or 0 when the haystack is exhausted without a match.
